notes.title: New level of gameplay! | HUGE update
notes.notes:
[h2]Ciao tutti![/h2]

We have released a [b]big update[/b] that will elevate your gameplay to a whole [b]new level[/b]! Adding [b]character progression[/b] with skill trees, special abilities, new cards and many QOL changes.

[h3][b]Let's dive in![/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=zlyzp7QFC9c;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Level Up![/h1]

First of all - let's talk about our main dish - [u][b]Character Progression[/b][/u]. This is a completely new mechanic, that will let your goons, waiters and cooks gain experience, and gain perks with each new level. You can combine several perks, or go further and unlock special abilities!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/44c79a39cb79135ed8573a7db9dae4b90d8eba52.gif[/img]

Your workers will gain XP every time they do their job. Cooks will get XP for making food, waiters for serving the clients, and goons for completing missions and winning battles against rival gangs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/7f32e18e03cdd33a8b900c82fb6e427e7aa5d55d.gif[/img]

Then, after one of your characters gain enough XP, a level-up card will get shuffled into your deck. Once you will use it - you'll see a skill tree and will be able to choose one of the options. There are quite juicy skills that you can pick, so keep these goons safe!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/c98ca73ee2ae574010b112fa2677e680a25a1259.gif[/img]

[h3]And there's more![/h3]

Here is the list of other changes and fixes present in this update

[b]Character progression:[/b]
- Added skill trees to employees.
- Added the ability to unlock new skills when leveling up.
- Added 12 new skills for employees.

[b]Misc:[/b]
- New patron skins.
- All dishes in the menu now divided into tiers.

[b]Bugfixes:[/b]
- Fixed police attention gauge.
- Fixed repeated upgrade cards draw.
- Fixed VIP cards bugging after winning a fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/136c4bef71172d948feea7e1042e184dd97eb782.gif[/img]

[h2]Tell us your feedback![/h2]

We are really excited to hear your feedback on this update! We worked hard to implement this new mechanic, and we are thrilled to hear your feedback in the Discussions. Thank you for staying with us and keep your eyes on the news!

notes.title: Update 1.0.2.6 | LOTS of changes!
notes.notes:
[h3]Buongiorno, famiglia![/h3]

It's been a while since our last update, but rest assured, we've been hard at work! We've made significant changes to the gameplay, introduced quality-of-life features, and we're closing in on completing our September Fixes list.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/c0844420a035b998b7e5e0471b1edfee3abc75eb.png[/img]

But first of all, [b]THANK YOU FOR YOUR FEEDBACK[/b]! 

We want to express our heartfelt gratitude to all our players for the invaluable feedback you've shared about the game. Your input is instrumental in our ongoing efforts to enhance the gaming experience. Thank you for being an essential part of our community!

Please, share your opinion on this update. It is critical for us to hear your feedback and improve the game even further.

[h2][b]Let's dive into the major changes![/b][/h2]

[b][h3]Economy changes[/h3][/b]
We've revamped the in-game economy to address the previous imbalance where players had great amounts of clean cash but struggled with black cash deficits, often leading to crippling debt in pre-IOU rework builds.

The tables have turned: now all salaries and upgrades are paid in clean cash, making it less available in the early game, while black cash is now primarily for laundering, as it should be. Some cards will still consume black cash, but you won't run out of it if you stay relatively active on the streets.

Of course, we can't show you all the balance changes in one GIF, you'll have to feel them in the game yourself.

We will keep on refining the game's balance, but we will need your opinion on these changes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/18ab577509eb3f811c350c2e7f51311cc9421632.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Bell indicator[/h3][/b]
We've introduced a special indicator above the deck, signaling when the next card you draw will feature a bell, eliminating the need to rely solely on luck.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/0daabd955f35bc992895aba404721fc936ba2665.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Boredom meter[/h3][/b]
Addressing concerns about gangster behavior, we've added a visual indicator that shows when a gangster is getting bored, helping you better manage their actions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/22552176d5732cddfc09742bf809228856bc137f.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Manual Battle Card activation[/h3][/b]
This feature was already integrated into the previous version. Now, you can click on a battle card to initiate combat instantly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/4c1c87864ee6c4daac232009fc8478734bf27f52.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Client's Order Bubbles[/h3][/b]
You can now see what your clients want to order as they approach their table, giving you clearer insight into the impact of your upgrades.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/650504dc49e9771ed23958aab80123690d73b822.gif[/img]

[b][h3]Tutorial Update[/h3][/b]
We've revamped the tutorial to provide new players with a better understanding of how event cards are activated and how the debt card functions. Try it out yourself!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/62db21a86b963c36555440ffc9a14d5a16d67ac3.gif[/img]

[b][h3]"Game Pause" Checkbox[/h3][/b]
We've included a new checkbox in the game settings called "App Pause." When disabled, the game won't pause when you switch to another window.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/d55d386715297150e803c47b3dbe4a104a5b1bb6.gif[/img]

This is a [b]big [/b] update and we are in dire need of feedback. Tell us what you think about it, because we won't stop refining the game until it is perfect. We do care about the game, and we care about your opinion on it.

See you in the future updates!

notes.notes:
Buon pomeriggio, signore e signori, we are [b]Königsborgs[/b], developers for [b]Don Duality[/b]. Here we go with the second part of our dev diaries!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/272ea4a03fc31b8a676bd78d5aa43b9fb3d45c0f.png[/img]

[h2][b]About similar games in terms of setting, gameplay and visuals[/b][/h2]
We can’t say there are similar games as [b]Don Duality[/b]. Honestly, the whole game was made on a clean slate without relying on any references. We initially thought about the experience we wanted to convey to the player - the duality of the life of a criminal, who in normal life seems to be a good citizen, but underground does dark deeds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/f40aa4fc2ab643748d69997cb79e9e21073f2d37.gif[/img]

[h2][b]About the challenges faced during the development[/b][/h2]
There were challenges mostly of a game design nature. [b]Don Duality[/b] is not similar to most tycoons (we can hardly put it in this category), so we had to invent a lot of things from scratch. It was also important for us to make all the player's actions through the cards as much as possible, no other way, so it was not easy to invent.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/d4f0e731a7d718c89734a6ec7c5e48940f20f4f1.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Some reasons to choose the GameMaker engine[/b][/h2]
Let's start with the fact that both coders in our team know this engine well enough to write virtually any 2D game. Besides, GameMaker is quite simple, reliable and can create builds for any technological platform.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/ca1a46460010f83936106a95e40b5a2b94aa38db.gif[/img]

[h2][b]What movies, TV series and books inspired us to create scenes in the game[/b][/h2]
The Sopranos, The Godfather, Ozark. Interestingly enough, at the time of the first game prototype development we were watching a TV series about money laundering. Perhaps it influenced the final idea of [b]Don Duality[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/4f1a2feb38e18ee4a0793c41ab3dd283d989a875.gif[/img]
[h2][b]About the created factions in the game[/b][/h2]
That was funny! Honestly, There was no plan. We just decided that the factions should be symmetrically placed in the corners of the map, so the game would be more balanced. We placed the districts themselves so that the distance between the factions would be about the same in conventional squares. So there is no magic here. Although, based on the faction archetypes, we tried to place them in areas that fit them better. I think you can easily read the factions by their appearance and name, as well as their starting locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/5805b8bfa7077ab36b80a4fe63cc54ba1f6921a5.gif[/img]

[h2][b]The biggest gameplay and visual changes throughout development[/b][/h2]
The biggest change is the mafia clan battle map. Although we originally planned something similar, in the initial plan we thought that there would be no other mafias on the map except for the Duality family, but in the end we came to the conclusion that initially the Duality family controlled the city and prevented other clans from taking the lead, but after the death of the father of the family, the Duality's position weakened a lot, as a result we have at the beginning of the game a state where all clans are about equal for the control of the city after a bloody war.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/9eaff1b0abc22e792102f8f9912d00ac3e154b88.gif[/img]

Grazie per your interest in our game, support and feedback! We look forward to your questions and thoughts!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/37aa67ce68b7a07c4abce50ad7482be51287d9c0.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Diary #1 | The duality of gamedev
notes.notes:
Hello friends, 

we are Königsborgs, [b]Don Duality[/b] devs. We would like to tell you about our game, its development and a bit about us! 

The team was formed spontaneously, during a jam, and includes the main programmer, who isn't even a gamemaker at all, the artist, the animator (he is only 15 years old!), the composer and, finally, the game designer. The game designer links the team together and, besides game design, he also deals with code and a bit of special effects. We can say that all of us in the team are self-taught.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/6f9d5a0764062280d69a68921493c23b3828bb30.png[/img]

And now, about our brainchild - [b]Don Duality[/b]! The idea for the game came right on the first day of the jam, as it usually happens. The concept of making a tycoon with mafia money laundering through a restaurant belonged to the main programmer of the project, and the game designer just added the card interaction mechanics. In two days we made a playable prototype and posted it on the jam site, but then completely forgot about it for a month.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/379823b3924fd51f4ea01227b5aa0c62399fb3cb.png[/img]
[i]One of the WIPs.[/i]

After a while we remembered [b]Don Duality[/b] and the Indie Cup festival, where in the end we decided to upload the improved version and even made the game trailer out of whatever we could. After a while our team started to receive cooperation offers, and the game was signed by the publisher Ravenage. 

The idea of the game is totally innovative. How can we describe [b]Don Duality[/b]? Originality. Addictiveness. Simple controls. As they say, easy to learn - hard to master.

The main difficulty is managing the balance. We're working on it all the time, and it's still not perfect. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43365106/05eedf65c8da58540d35ce47387198a5a1882e45.png[/img]
[i]The way the game looks now.[/i]

The setting was born from the game's theme of "duality." So, the title occurred literally as soon as we thought about the mafia and the restaurant. The Italian trace is more of a popular trope associated with the image of the Mafia. There is no direct inspiration for the game, although it is the mechanics with events that we took from the board game Hunted. Some of the events will have references to the real ones or from the movies.  I dare say that [b]Don Duality[/b] is a new genre that combines a card game, management, and strategy.
